effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative findings cover both district-level water rights/groundwater reliance and Wilcoxon comparisons of disadvantaged communities inside vs. outside irrigation district boundaries.
effect_estimate.value: 60% of irrigation districts with senior pre-1914 surface water rights hold surface water allocations equal to twice (and up to three times) their crop water demand, whereas 86% of San Joaquin Valley irrigation districts rely on groundwater for irrigation (12% exclusively), and evaluating 2001-2015 average surface water deliveries rather than paper allocations increases groundwater-dependent districts by 32%. Across disadvantaged communities (unpaired two-sample Wilcoxon test), communities inside irrigation district boundaries (ID-DACs, n = 97) do not have better drinking water or vulnerability outcomes than groundwater-dependent communities outside district boundaries (GDCs, n = 56): mean poor drinking water exposure percentile is 83% vs. 79% (p = 0.1363), threats to groundwater percentile is 56% vs. 55% (p = 0.829), overall DAC vulnerability is 83% vs. 81% (p = 0.3147), poverty is 83% vs. 84% (p = 0.1166), and median household income is $34,276 vs. $36,450 (p = 0.7893), while ID-DACs experience significantly higher pollution exposure (81% vs. 74%, p = 0.005413) and pesticide exposure (83% vs. 77%, p = 0.00965) and smaller mean populations (9,899 vs. 20,515, p = 0.003456).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 11, Section 3.2; PDF p. 13, Section 3.3 and Table 1; PDF p. 17, Section 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Observational cross-sectional geospatial and statistical study (capped at <= 2 by design ceiling). Coded as 1 because the study documents descriptive and statistical associations between legal/institutional variables (historical water rights era/pre-1914 status and location inside vs. outside irrigation district service boundaries) and water supply/drinking-water exposure outcomes without directly observing administrative connection, permitting, or community-level service provision processes.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 8-10, Sections 2.2-2.4; PDF p. 10-14, Sections 3.1-3.3 and Table 1

sample_size.comment: Exact sample sizes are reported for the disadvantaged community comparison (n = 97 ID-DACs and n = 56 GDCs) across 8 San Joaquin Valley counties; the exact total count of irrigation districts is not printed in the main text (full district table deposited in Dryad/Supporting Information, with partial cluster counts given for 3 of 5 clusters in Section 3.4: 27 FCC, 14 SCG [13 Hydraulic Era + 1 pre-1914], and 7 SSN).
sample_size.value: 153 disadvantaged communities (97 irrigation district disadvantaged communities [ID-DACs] and 56 groundwater-dependent communities [GDCs]); irrigation districts across 8 San Joaquin Valley counties (exact total number of irrigation districts not stated in main text; partial cluster counts reported for 3 of 5 clusters: 27 FCC, 14 SCG, 7 SSN)

study_design.comment: Combines historical era grouping, gridded water-balance modeling (WAFR), cluster analysis of irrigation districts, and cross-sectional two-sample Wilcoxon comparisons of socioeconomic and environmental indicators across census-place DACs.
study_design.value: Observational cross-sectional geospatial and sociohydrological study (historical era analysis, gridded water-budget modeling, cluster analysis of irrigation districts, and two-sample Wilcoxon comparison of disadvantaged communities)
